::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** 14 May 1872  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford.
:::

My dear [Elizabeth](people/person_1566.qmd)
I feel such a strong inclination to call you so and to think I have known you all your life that I do not think I shall balk myself at the risk of appearing to you both a gushing and impertinent old lady. NB – I have first read a letter from a contemporary – a year younger talking of her three great nieces also of gout and rheumaticism Isn’t that enough to make one feel venerable? But somehow I did feel to get on with you in a wonderful way. I think the deep spirit of veneration made on feel you like the dear ones I grew up with. I wished you had been here to read [Mr Wither](people/person_1544.qmd)’s comment on hearing you were here ‘[C Lincoln](people/person_1565.qmd) is a noble Bishop, I am glad you have one of his daughters under your roof’[^1] I also wanted you to be here to see a letter from [Mr Codrington](people/person_312.qmd) from Queensland, with the further particulars he had gathered, though he has not yet seen the two Mota men [John](people/person_2284.qmd) and [James](people/person_2283.qmd).[^2] The first indication of the dreadful tetanus coming on with [Mr Atkin](people/person_1979.qmd) was his sticking at a word while administering the Bread at that last Sunday Celebration, and then the Mota men knew what would follow![[footnote: [Stephen](people/person_1279.qmd)’s whole behaviour was martyr like, always reading his Gospels and prayerbook in the intervals of the Convulsions. I found this copy of Mr Atkin’s letter printed in the N L [?]- I have another copy, so you need not return it.[^3] An Eton master – one of our many cousins has turned up as [Mr Elgie](people/person_478.qmd)’s substitute, so as I have not heard from you I am rather glad to conclude that your brother would not like it. Five girls, of whom two at least like parish work are a good look out for the schools.[^4]

Yours affectionately
C M Young

---

[^1]: The former curate of Otterbourne, the Rev. William Bigg-Wither.  ‘C.Lincoln’ would have been Bishop Wordsworth’s signature.
[^2]: CMY refers to the death of [Bishop Patteson](people/person_1155.qmd). His assistant the Rev. Robert Henry Codrington (1830-1922),  refused the bishopric of Melanesia after his death but was head of the mission 1871-77.
[^3]: CMY's biography of Patteson records that between his being wounded and the tetanus coming on Atkin read her novel *The Chaplet of Pearls*.
[^4]: The Rev. [John Eyre Yonge](people/person_1620.qmd) (1818-1890), first cousin to CMY, had six daughters, of whom one married in 1872.  The Rev. Walter Francis Elgie (d.1881), curate of Otterbourne, was probably ill or on holiday.
